upstream.scope: Multiple isolated host windows (D1 §§6.2–6.3, 17–18; D2 T23–T24, T38): the generic connection manager runs several sessions at once, each in its own ConnectionSessionContext and attempt generation, and every window names its host, account and incarnation (session_id) in client-owned chrome. Two hosts serving identical node IDs, PIDs, names and item identities share no selection, event sequence, cached identity or confirmation; replacing one session leaves the other intact. No protocol message, registry entry, SDK, runtime or srtop product change; no new dependency. No side-by-side metric comparison view and no cross-host action

entries.feature: Several connections run concurrently, each in its own ConnectionSessionContext keyed by the saved entry: its own replica (TransactionApplier: cached rows and ItemIds), EventOutbox (client_instance_id, event_seq, pending events), ResourceCache, TransactionIngressGate, SessionContinuityContext and AppKitRenderer (render objects, selection memory, collection caches), and its own attempt generation (activeTokens); two hosts serving the same fixture (same node IDs, PIDs 4101/4102, names and ItemIds) keep their selections and outbox sequences apart, natively over two real localhost SSH sessions

Every Surface window of a session carries a client-owned identity line, a titlebar accessory apart from the server's title and PX-022-G01's status subtitle: '<user>@<host>[:port] · session <session_id> · saved as “<label>”' (the endpoint first; the local name only when it differs from it; 'no session attached yet' before the first ready; 'session with an invalid ID' for a server-reported ID that fails SavedConnection.validSessionID); it follows ready and REPLACED decisions, reaches every window mounted later (remounts, the confirmation's commit), is reachable by VoiceOver as one static text element, and each entry's windows get their own tabbingIdentifier so no tab group spans two sessions

A confirmation stays bound to one session: its panel is in the window that names its host, account and session; another session's controller refuses its node before anything is allocated or sent (the node is not in that replica); and another srtop instance with identical processes, holding its own pending request for the same PID in the same slot, rejects it (REJECTED, 'event target node … does not exist in store') because every run draws its own panel range (PX-031), leaving its own intent pending

Replacing, reconnecting, failing or removing one connection leaves the other session intact: its status stays connected, its attempt is never stopped, its replica, window, identity, selection and pending intent are unchanged; natively, a restarted srtop on host A (a new incarnation, REPLACED) rebuilds A's window while B stays connected throughout and later confirms its own intent

Alerts stay bound to their connection: a new attempt dismisses only its own connection's alert (or one naming no connection), never another host's; another connection's alert folded into a Session Replaced disclosure names its endpoint; the Session Replaced message names the endpoint whose session was replaced
